hypotheses.H1_kl_behavior: KL-only distillation improves FineWeb KL relative to activation-refined CP-2048 without worsening either OOD KL by more than 0.005.
hypotheses.H2_causal_training: Causal distillation improves Fisher effect fidelity for both preregistered intervention families relative to activation-refined CP-2048.
hypotheses.H3_tensor_anchor: A 0.01 tensor anchor improves isotropic tensor fidelity without costing more than 0.005 mean KL or 0.05 causal fidelity relative to unanchored causal distillation.
hypotheses.H4_scale_transfer: Any causal improvement appears at held-out intervention scales and on both OOD corpora, rather than only at the sampled training condition.
hypotheses.H5_causal_gate: At least one trained model reaches 0.90 Fisher effect fidelity and 0.95 effect cosine for Gaussian 0.10 and natural-mix 0.25 interventions.

hypotheses.H1_manifold_gap: Activation-refined CP-2048 has better natural-language fidelity but worse isotropic tensor fidelity than direct CP-2048.
hypotheses.H2_causal_gap: The behavioral advantage of activation-refined CP-2048 over direct CP-2048 shrinks under held-out MLP-input interventions or OOD text.
hypotheses.H3_sparse_conditional_program: Mixed routed CP-2048/K128 uses no more than 6.25% of factors per token while using more than half of the dictionary across a corpus.
hypotheses.H4_collective_over_component_stability: Cross-objective activation-space similarity is substantially higher than median individual CP-term similarity.
hypotheses.H5_semantic_transfer: Factors selected on FineWeb for token-form categories retain an oriented mean held-out AUROC above 0.60 on both OOD corpora.
hypotheses.H6_no_current_full_pass: No existing decomposition passes all behavioral, OOD, causal, and parsimony gates simultaneously.
